content:
The late singer Dolly Parton's sister Stella Parton discussed why her younger sister chose not to publicly reveal her cancer diagnosis in a new interview that aired on Thursday.

"Dolly could never tolerate negativity, and she certainly didn't want her fans worrying about her," the 77-year-old Stella Parton said with a smile to Gayle King on 'CBS Mornings'. "She also didn't want too many people in the family worrying about her."

She said: "Some of us knew — those who were closer to her," but added that "not every relative" was informed.

When King asked whether the 80-year-old Dolly Parton had kept her condition secret to avoid worrying people, her sister replied firmly, "Absolutely."

However, out of respect for the country music icon's wishes, she did not reveal what type of cancer Dolly Parton had.

Stella Parton said: "It's not my story to tell."

When King asked what she would miss most about her sister, Stella Parton said it was "her optimism".

"She is the most optimistic person I have ever known," she said, but added: "I won't remember her in suffering."

She said she felt her sister passed away "with a peaceful heart".

Stella Parton said: "She knew where she was going. She wasn't going to a bad place — she was going to be with Mom and Dad. She was absolutely ready."

Dolly Parton's nephew shared an emotional video on social media last month announcing the singer's passing. Her representative later confirmed that the star of '9 to 5' had lost her battle after a "brief fight with cancer".
